newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - M&S sees similar costs for 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - M&S sees similar costs for 1997/98.

text.p: British retailer Marks and Spencer Plc said on Tuesday the outlook on costs for the current year will be similar to last year.
Chairman Sir Richard Greenbury said the group will take on about 1,700 more staff in Britain in 1997/98 because the group's expansion programme required more staff.

But he said costs would not rise faster than sales. "People are concerned that when we take on extra staff the costs will rise faster than the sales but they haven't done that," he told Reuters in an interview.
Greenbury said the return on sales last year was held at about 14 percent, which he said was one of the highest in the world.
When asked about the prospect of a minimum wage being introduced in Britain, Greenbury said he was not worried.

"Whatever happens...if you include both the bonus at Christmas and the non contributory pension, we're paying over six pounds an hour. So it doesn't really worry me where it's set even if it happens."
He said M&S would be telling its staff what pay increase they will receive for the current year later this morning.
The retailer expects to add around 460,000 square feet of space in Britain this year as part of a 1.5 billion stg expansion programme over the next three years.

Greenbury said the money would be spread across the UK and continental Europe. "The bulk of it will be in growing our UK business and of course looking for the 30 or 40 sites that we want in Europe." He said this would be in Germany, France and Spain."
Last year M&S's capital expenditure reached a record 426 million stg.

Greenbury said in Britain, where M&S has 286 outlets, the group planned to add selling space by extending existing stores by 260,000 square feet, and opening new stores with a total of 200,000 square feet at Cribbs Causeway in Bristol and Newry in Northern Ireland.
He said there were still opportunities to expand in Britain even though M&S was in most town centres and most edge and out of town situations that it wanted to be in.
"There's always opportunities coming along here and there," he said.

When asked if M&S would be interested in buying stores put up for sale by retailing group Littlewoods. Greenbury said there were a few very interesting sites, but M&S did not want to buy the entire business.
"They've got one or two very interesting sites, but they're tyring to sell the business as a going concern."
Greenbury said if Littlewoods were to change its approach M&S would probably think again.
The group said in food, the UK environment was fiercely competitive, but M&S held market share and maintained margins.
Greenbury said UK retailing was competitive in general.
"It's a very, very competitive environment in clothing, in foods, in retailing generally. In every single area its competitive," he said.
He said M&S increased market share in clothing and home furnishing and held market share in food "to the decimal point."

M&S's clothing market share is around 16 to 17 percent. "We posted a nine and half percent increase and national clothing sales in same 52 weeks are 6.1 percent ahead..... we've obviously gained market share," he said.
Earlier M&S reported an 11 percent increase in annual profits to 1.1 billion stg. Its shares were 4.5 pence lower at 504.5 pence by 0925 GMT.
-- Jane Merriman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
